title: private-installer: add `backup create` command (manifest + encrypted artifact + verification output)
author: Benji Okafor
description: This PR introduces an initial `backup create` workflow in the Redwood Private installer CLI to support Day-2 operations and DR readiness. The command produces (1) a human-readable manifest (JSON) describing what was captured and how it was encrypted, and (2) an encrypted artifact (tarball) containing the control-plane state snapshot files and selected deterministic configuration inputs. The goal of this PR is to ship the core mechanics (consistent snapshot + packaging + encryption + basic verification/logging) so Solutions/SRE teams can begin rehearsing restores in staging while we iterate on storage backends, scheduled jobs, and restore automation. Scope: control-plane backup only (no data-plane model cache / no customer prompt data). Secrets are not exported as raw secret material; we only record references (e.g., external KMS key ARNs, secret names) and require the target cluster to have access to the same secret sources at restore time. The artifact format is intentionally versioned (`format_version: 1`) and includes integrity checks (SHA256) for each included file and the encrypted blob. Encryption is implemented as AES-256-GCM with a randomly generated data key; for this PR, the data key is derived from a user-provided passphrase via scrypt and stored only in-memory during packaging (no plaintext key material written to disk). A follow-up will add a KMS provider interface for envelope encryption (see ENG-9823) and backup storage backends (S3/NFS) integration. Operator UX: `redwood-private backup create --output ./backups --cluster-context <ctx> [--include-etcd-snapshot=auto] [--quiesce-timeout=60s]` prints a summary, writes `manifest.json` and `backup-<cluster>-<ts>.tar.enc`, and optionally runs a post-backup verification step that re-reads the artifact header and validates checksums. Logging: adds structured log lines with `backup_id`, `duration_ms`, `bytes_written`, and `error_category` for future metrics wiring. Documentation: adds CLI help text and a short internal README section describing the artifact layout and the restore prerequisites. Known limitations (explicitly documented in help output): (a) does not back up Kubernetes resources/CRDs (Velero integration is tracked separately), (b) etcd snapshot capture is best-effort and gated behind `--include-etcd-snapshot` because some Private installs do not grant direct etcd access, (c) no remote upload; output is a local directory only, (d) no key rotation / KMS-based sealing yet. This aligns with ADR-027 direction (manifest + encrypted bundle + deterministic layout), but the key management details are expected to change once KMS provider lands; the format_version is reserved for that evolution.
commits: cli: add `backup` command group + `backup create` subcommand
backup: implement snapshot planner for control-plane components
backup: add artifact writer (tar + manifest + checksums) and encryptor
logging: standardize backup/restore log fields + error categories
docs: add installer README section for backup artifact layout
tests: add unit tests for manifest schema + checksum verification
testing: Unit tests: `go test ./...` (added focused tests for manifest serialization, checksum generation, and decrypt+verify path using a fixed nonce in test-only helper). Manual: validated on staging cluster `stg-private-3` by running `redwood-private backup create --output /tmp/rw-backups --include-etcd-snapshot=off` and confirming (1) artifact + manifest written, (2) summary printed, (3) `--verify` reports PASS, (4) failure modes produce actionable error_category (permissions, missing kubecontext, insufficient disk).
review_conversation: Ethan Park: The include list mentions `routing-policies`. Where are those sourced from? We should be explicit that we’re backing up control-plane DB state + installer-known config, not live K8s objects. Also please add a format_version to the manifest so we can evolve encryption without breaking restores.

Benji Okafor (author): Routing policies are persisted in the config DB and surfaced via the control-plane API; this implementation snapshots the DB, and the manifest component list is descriptive (not a source-of-truth inventory). I added `format_version: 1` and clarified in help text that K8s resources are out of scope for this command.

Sean Gallagher: For on-call usability, we need deterministic filenames and a stable location for `latest`. Also, log output should include duration and bytes; future dashboards will rely on it. Can we also avoid printing anything that looks like key material?

Benji Okafor (author): Added deterministic filename template `backup-<cluster>-<timestamp>.tar.enc` and `manifest-<backup_id>.json`. I held off on a `latest` symlink because Windows/on-prem customers may not have it; instead we print the output paths and backup_id. Logging now includes `duration_ms`/`bytes_written` and we never log salt/nonce or passphrase-derived data.

Hanae Suzuki: Please double-check the crypto: AES-GCM nonce reuse would be catastrophic. Make sure nonce is random per artifact and not derived from timestamp. Also, can we add guardrails so the artifact never includes raw Kubernetes Secret values?

Benji Okafor (author): Nonce is generated from `crypto/rand` per artifact; tests use fixed nonce in a test-only helper. Added an explicit denylist in the planner: we will not read `Secret` data from the cluster; we only snapshot application datastores + config files and record secret *references* in the manifest when applicable.

Connor O'Brien: Packaging question: we’ll need this to work in air-gapped flows later. Please keep the output fully self-contained, and don’t add implicit network calls. Also, ensure we can verify integrity offline.

Benji Okafor (author): No network calls in this PR. Verification is offline: we hash files pre-encryption, hash the encrypted blob, and emit those in the manifest. `--verify` reads the artifact header and validates checksums without external dependencies.

Kira Thompson: The CLI help reads like a runbook; keep it concise but include prerequisites and a link to the Confluence runbook once it exists. Also, add an example command with `--quiesce-timeout` since that’s a common customer ask.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated help text to a concise prerequisites list + example commands, and added TODO link placeholder for Confluence page (will be replaced when docs land).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into `main` by Connor O'Brien after approvals from Ethan Park and Sean Gallagher. Squash commit message: "Add backup create command to private installer (manifest + encrypted artifact)".
release_notes: Private installer now supports `redwood-private backup create` to generate a versioned manifest and encrypted backup artifact suitable for staging DR rehearsals. No external storage backends or KMS envelope encryption in this release.
